_comment: Configuration for sources/watch.py. Two discovery channels, each switchable.
The watchlist channel is derived from sources/manifest.json and needs no
configuration beyond the dossier guard. The topic channel is the query that
finds acts nobody told us to look for, and it is the one that needs tuning.
Follows what the manifest already tracks: other documents in the same
procedure dossier, and newer consolidations of the prior rules a tracked
act amends.
max_dossier_members is a guard, not a preference. CELLAR files a work
under two kinds of dossier: the procedure dossier (the proposal plus its
staff working documents, ~4-8 members) and a broad Commission-level
dossier that pools hundreds of unrelated files -- the one holding the ETS
proposal also holds securitisation, defence procurement, and gas storage.
Following the broad one would drown the agent in its first run, so any
dossier above this size is skipped and reported.
A narrow EuroVoc query. Narrow is the point: this channel exists to catch
acts outside the manifest, and a wide query makes every run a triage bill
with a low hit rate. These concepts are the ones the tracked acts are
themselves indexed under, which is the most defensible starting set.

Widen deliberately and one concept at a time, watching the in/out ratio in
the run report. If a run returns dozens of candidates and almost all triage
as out, the last concept added was too broad.
2026-08-18: four circularity concepts added at once, which breaks the
one-at-a-time rule deliberately and for a stated reason. The register now
carries PPWR, and the Circular Economy Act is the named capture priority --
but the five emissions concepts above would not have surfaced either. Yield
since 2025 is 106 works under circular economy, 83 waste management, 68
waste recycling, 38 packaging; overlapping heavily, and roughly 6 a month
against a 40-per-run breaker. Watch the in/out ratio and cut back if it is
poor.
KNOWN LIMIT, and it is the important one: CELLAR had indexed 32025R0040
under NO EuroVoc concept at all when this was checked, seven months after
publication. The topic channel would therefore have missed PPWR however it
was tuned. EuroVoc indexing lags publication, so this channel cannot be the
only defence for an act we already know is coming -- see the CEA entry in
queued.json.
Which CELEX shapes are candidates at all. This is a cheap structural
filter applied before triage, so it must only exclude things that are out
of scope by their document type rather than their content.
Sector 3 is adopted legislation, sector 5 is Commission preparatory
documents. Within sector 5, PC is a proposal for an act and is in; SC is a
staff working document and DC is a communication -- scope.md rules both
out by type, so they are dropped here rather than paid for at triage.
Sector 3 needs the same treatment. Its descriptor letter is the
instrument: L directive, R regulation, D decision -- all binding, all in.
H is a recommendation and A an opinion, neither of which imposes anything;
the first live run surfaced two methane-regulation recommendations that
sailed past an unfiltered sector 3.
effort is medium rather than low because the judgment is legal, not
clerical: the classifier is deciding whether a title like 'determining
revised benchmark values' creates an obligation. The cost of a wrong 'out'
is a measure that silently never enters the register.
max_candidates_per_run is a circuit breaker. A widened query or a CELLAR
backfill can return hundreds of candidates; rather than spend that, the
run stops and reports, and a human decides whether the query was wrong.
